lines.li: [them] Whoever walked with us after dark could have brought a coat.
[us,lowtech] We're used to the cold here, and we see well enough by the stars.
[us] We're used to the cold here, but I'll pass it on.
[them] Your people watched my packs after dark more closely than my own guards do.
[us] We'd hate for anything of yours to go missing here.
[them] So would I, which is why I noticed.
[them] At court, a companion after dark is either a courtesy or a spy.
[us] Which was ours?
[them,tone:warm|tone:good] A courtesy, I have decided, and I will hold to it.
[them] I have not decided yet.
[them] Among my people, one who follows a guest in the dark is called a wolf.
[us] Here we'd call it keeping the guest company.
[them] The elders would laugh at that, and so do I.
[them] Do your people walk every guest around after dark, or only me?
[us] Only the ones who stay up late, and you stayed up late.
[them] I'll go to bed earlier, then.
[them] One of yours kept us company after dark, which was welcome on a strange night.
[us] Guests shouldn't wander a place they don't know alone.
[them,their:lowtech] My grandmother would have said you were watching us, and she'd have been right.
[them] It felt safer, I'll say that.
[them] Do you always walk behind your guests at night?
[us] Only the ones who walk about at night.
[them] Then I'll stay put.
[them] Call off whoever you had trailing me after dark.
[us] You're a guest here, and guests are looked after.
[them] Someone of yours stood out in the wet with us after dark and never said why.
[us] Better two wet than one lost.
[them] I wasn't lost.
[them] I'm used to being watched at home, I didn't expect it here as well.
[us] Someone of your standing gets looked after.
[them,their:empire] Looked after is the word the court uses too.
[them] That's one way to put it.
[them] You again, with your questions.
[us] Only a greeting this time.
[them] First the questions, and now you walk behind me at night.
[us] It's what the council asks of me.
[them] I know that now, yes.
[them] I've told my people what you were asking about, so don't bother asking them.
[us] I'll ask about the weather, then.
[them] Do that.
[them] I was angry about the questions your colony asked about us.
[us] And now?
[them,trait:Kind] Now I think everyone looks out for their own, and so did you.
[them] Now I'm less angry, and that will have to do.
[us] It's more than we had a right to expect.
[them] Your colony went asking about one of ours, and traders hear everything.
[us] Traders hear a great deal that isn't so.
[them] Not this time.
[them] At court, questions like your keeper's would have cost a title.
[us] There are no titles to lose in our keeper's seat.
[them] The cost is in what we now think of your colony.
[them] The elders say one who asks too many questions at the fire wants something.
[us] Everyone wants something.
[them] Not everyone hides it.
[them] In our town your keeper of secrets would have spent a day in the stocks.
[us] Then I'm glad it was only words.
[them] Words cost your colony plenty with us, believe me.
[them] Your colony ran its own background check on us, and we noticed.
[us] We like to know our neighbors.
[them] Then ask us, like neighbors.
[them] What your colony asked of me is behind us, as far as I'm concerned.
[us] I'm glad to hear it.
[them] Don't make me sorry I said so.
[them] I remember what your colony asked of me, and the price it named.
[us] It was the council's doing.
[them] Then the council can remember it too.
[them] I've nothing to say to a colony that bargains with other people's shame.
[us] Then say nothing, and we'll both be easier.
[them] At court one learns to pay for silence, and never to forgive whoever named the price.
[us] It was named once, and it won't be again.
[them] I shall believe that when I have seen it.
[them] The spirits saw what your colony asked of me, and they keep count.
[us] They've seen worse, I'm sure.
[them] Not from neighbors.
[them] You'll understand if I don't stay at your table long.
[us] Stay as long or as short as you like.
[them] Short, then.
[them] Our people know what {WRONGNAME} kept quiet now, and they heard it from your colony.
[us] {WRONGNAME} was given the chance to keep it quiet.
[them] For a price, which makes it worse.
[them] Your colony spread word of what one of our people kept hidden.
[us] They had the chance to keep it hidden.
[them] At a price your colony set.
[them] Your colony trades in other people's shame, so keep your distance.
[us] Suit yourself.
[them] Everywhere I stop, they've heard how your colony treated one of ours.
[us] People will talk about anything on the road.
[them] They talk about this more than most.
[them] What your colony told about one of ours did harm, and I still think it was wrong.
[us] I won't argue with you about it.
[them] Good, because I like you, and I'd rather not.
[them] Among our people, carrying a tale is worse than the thing it tells.
[us] Then I'm sorry it was carried.
[them] Sorry doesn't carry it back.
[them,task:you] Your words reach our elders' fire every few days.
[them] Your {OFFICE}'s words reach our elders' fire every few days.
[us,task:you] I have a lot to say, and I try to keep it kind.
[us] {OFFICER} has a lot to say, and most of it is kind.
[them] The elders listen to the kind parts twice.
[them,task:you] Your letters are read out in our hall, seal and all.
[them] Your {OFFICE}'s letters are read out in our hall, seal and all.
[us,task:you] I'd have written more carefully if I'd known that.
[us] I hope {OFFICER} spells everyone's names right, at least.
[them] Most of them.
[them,task:you] Our head keeps your letters in a folder that's getting thick.
[them] Our head keeps your {OFFICE}'s letters in a folder that's getting thick.
[us] Thick is good, I hope.
[them] Thick means read, which is more than most mail gets.
[them,task:you] Your messages are filed, flagged and answered, in that order.
[them] Your {OFFICE}'s messages are filed, flagged and answered, in that order.
[us] That's more ceremony than I expected.
[them] Flagged is the part that matters.
[them,task:you] You write with a courtesy one rarely finds outside the court.
[them] Your {OFFICE} writes with a courtesy one rarely finds outside the court.
[us,task:you] I learned the forms, and I mean them.
[us,us:noble] Some of the court's habits came with us out here.
[us] {OFFICER} works hard at those letters.
[them] It shows, and it is noticed.
[them,task:you] If you're courting our people, remember that heads change.
[them] If your {OFFICE} is courting our people, remember that heads change.
[us] And heirs remember who wrote to them?
[them] Heirs remember who didn't.
[them,task:you] You write to us as if we were old friends.
[them] Your {OFFICE} writes to us as if we were old friends.
[us] We'd like to be.
[them] Letters alone won't do it.
[them] You're the one who writes to us, aren't you?
[us] Every few days, and I hope it isn't a burden.
[them,task:visited] Not at all, and since you came yourself people ask after you by name.
[them] Not at all, people ask when the next letter is coming.
[us] Then I'll keep writing.
[them,task:you] You came to see us in the cold months, and that is remembered.
[them] Your {OFFICE} came to see us in the cold months, and that is remembered.
[us,task:you] It was a cold road, and a warm welcome at the end of it.
[us] {OFFICER} said the welcome made up for the road.
[them] Our people wanted it to.
[them,task:you] You asked my prices before I'd even unpacked.
[them] Your {OFFICE} asked my prices before I'd even unpacked.
[us,task:you] I like to know where we stand before the bargaining starts.
[us] {OFFICER} likes to know where we stand.
[them] Fair enough, I like a buyer who's done the sums.
[them,task:you] You ask which hides we keep and which we trade away.
[them] Your {OFFICE} asks which hides we keep and which we trade away.
[us] We want to know what you'd take for them.
[them] The elders will want to see your goods before they say.
[them,task:you] Our market reeve has your letters pinned up beside the scales.
[them] Our market reeve has your {OFFICE}'s letters pinned up beside the scales.
[us] I hope that's good for trade.
[them] It's good for gossip, and trade follows gossip.
[them,task:you] You want our price list, and our buyers want yours.
[them] Your {OFFICE} wants our price list, and our buyers want yours.
[us] Then let's swap them.
[them] Send yours first, buyers never go first.
[them,task:you] Your inquiry is in our purchasing queue.
[them] Your {OFFICE}'s inquiry is in our purchasing queue.
[us] Is that a yes?
[them] It's a maybe, and for our buyers that's warm.
[them,task:you] You spent a whole day going over what our people buy and sell.
[them] Your {OFFICE} spent a whole day going over what our people buy and sell.
[us,task:you] And I came home with a list as long as my arm.
[us] {OFFICER} came home with a list as long as my arm.
[them] We hope something comes of it.
[them,task:you] If you want to know what sells at home, start with what we're short of.
[them] If your {OFFICE} wants to know what sells at home, start with what we're short of.
[us] Which is?
[them,town:short:food] Food, this season more than any.
[them,town:short:medicine] Medicine, and plenty of it.
[them,town:short:fuel] Anything that burns.
[us,task:you] I'll remember that.
[us] I'll tell {OFFICER}.
[them,task:you] If you drill our fighters, our band will be the better for it when you call.
[them] If your {OFFICE} drills our fighters, our band will be the better for it when you call.
[us] That's the idea.
[them,task:you] Then we'll make room for you in the yard.
[them] Then we'll make room in the yard for {OFFICER}.
[them,task:you] Our young hunters argue over who will face you first.
[them] Our young hunters argue over who will face your {OFFICE} first.
[us,task:you] I'll want them in a line, not one at a time.
[us] {OFFICER} will want them in a line, not one at a time.
[them] They'll learn, after the arguing.
[them,task:you] Our men at arms are polishing their helmets for your visit.
[them] Our men at arms are polishing their helmets for your {OFFICE}'s visit.
[us,task:you] I'll want them in the mud, not shining.
[us] {OFFICER} will want them in the mud, not shining.
[them] They know, they just like to look the part first.
[them,task:you] Our security lead wants your drill plan sent ahead.
[them] Our security lead wants your {OFFICE}'s drill plan sent ahead.
[us,task:you] Most of it's in my head, but I'll write it down.
[us] {OFFICER} will bring it in person.
[them] Then we'll clear a day for it.
[them,task:you] We heard about the raid on your walls, so you must have things to teach.
[them] We heard about the raid on your walls, so your {OFFICE} must have things to teach.
[us] Some of them learned the hard way.
[them] That's the way that sticks.
[them,task:you] The sick at home ask after you every morning.
[them] The sick at home ask after your {OFFICE} every morning.
[us,task:you] I mean to come, with whatever the stores can spare.
[us] {OFFICER} means to come, with whatever the stores can spare.
[them] Then we'll keep a bed by the door.
[them,task:you] Do you know the sickness could follow you home?
[them] Does your {OFFICE} know the sickness could follow them home?
[us,task:you] I know, and I'm coming anyway.
[us] {OFFICER} knows, and means to come anyway.
[them,task:you] Then we owe you more than thanks.
[them] Then we owe {OFFICER} more than thanks.
[them] Our healers have burned every herb they know, and the sick are no better.
[us,task:you] I'll bring what we have.
[us] Our {OFFICE} will bring what we have.
[them] The elders will remember who came.
[them,task:you] Our medics are stretched thin, so whatever you bring will be used.
[them] Our medics are stretched thin, so whatever your {OFFICE} brings will be used.
[us] It won't be much, but it'll be good.
[them] Good is what we need.
[them,task:you] Your letters about the one we hold are very firm.
[them] Your {OFFICE}'s letters about the one we hold are very firm.
[us] They're meant to be.
[them] We read them, and we'll name a price all the same.
[them] The one of yours we hold is eating well, if that helps.
[us] It helps, and we want them home.
[them,task:you] You've made that plain, and our head is listening.
[them] Your {OFFICE} has made that plain, and our head is listening.
[them] You're the one who keeps writing about your colonist.
[us] And I'll keep writing until they're home.
[them] I'll tell our head, it may move things along.
[them,task:you] You wrote that our people in your cells are fed and kept warm.
[them] Your {OFFICE} wrote that our people in your cells are fed and kept warm.
[us] They are, every day.
[them] Their families read that letter more than once.
[them] Letters about our people won't make up for the bars.
[us] Make an offer, then, and they're yours.
[them] Before I go, tell me the ones in your cells are treated decently.
[us,task:you] They are, and I write to your head about them myself.
[us] They are, and our {OFFICE} writes to your head about them.
[them] I'll carry that home, it's something.
[them,task:you] Your letters are read at our rites now, beside our own words.
[them] Your {OFFICE}'s letters are read at our rites now, beside our own words.
[us] It's good to pray for the same things.
[them,their:tribal] The elders say two fires praying the same way give one light.
[them] It is, and good to know someone else does.
[them,task:you] Your letters have been a comfort since our loss.
[them] Your {OFFICE}'s letters have been a comfort since our loss.
[us,task:you] I'm glad, I didn't know whether to write of it.
[us] {OFFICER} writes from the heart.
[them] It showed.
[them] You write to us as someone who prays the way we do.
[us] Because I do.
[them] Then you're welcome at our rites whenever you come.
[them,task:you] You prayed with us when you came, and our people remember it.
[them] Your {OFFICE} prayed with us when they came, and our people remember it.
[us,task:you] I came home steadier than I left.
[us] {OFFICER} came home steadier than they left.
[them] So did we, after.
[them,task:you] Every letter you send about your faith starts an argument at our table.
[them] Every letter your {OFFICE} sends about your faith starts an argument at our table.
[us] Arguments are a start.
[them] That's what worries some of us.
[them,task:you] We have our own faith, and you keep writing as if we didn't.
[them] We have our own faith, and your {OFFICE} keeps writing as if we didn't.
[us,task:you] I mean well.
[us] {OFFICER} means well.
[them] Meaning well is easy.
[them] Some of what your {OFFICE} writes has been talked over at our table for days.
[us] That's all {OFFICER} hopes for.
[them] Don't tell {OFFICER} that, it would only bring more letters.
[them,task:you] Those who keep our rites have read your letters, and they aren't pleased.
[them] Those who keep our rites have read your {OFFICE}'s letters, and they aren't pleased.
[us] Not pleased, or not persuaded?
[them] Both, and they say so at every rite.
[them] Our people are coming to your feast, and already arguing over who sits where.
[us,task:you] I have the same trouble with our own.
[us] Our {OFFICE} has the same trouble.
[them,their:lowtech] Seat our head by the fire and the rest of us will sit anywhere.
[them] Seat our head well and the rest of us will sit anywhere.
[them] Our hunters will bring what they can to your feast, it's our way.
[us] There'll be plenty, bring yourselves.
[them] Guests who bring nothing aren't guests among us.
[them] Will there be music at your feast, or only food?
[us,task:you] I'm working on the music.
[us] {OFFICER} is seeing to all of it.
[them] At court, a feast without music is only a long meal.
[them] So you're the one who'll be feeding us.
[us] Feeding you, seating you, and keeping the peace at the table.
[them] That's three jobs.
[us] It feels like more.
[them] A feast in the cold months is a generous thing.
[us,poor] Our stores aren't full, but we'll set a good table.
[us] Our stores will stand it.
[them] Then we'll come hungry and leave grateful.
[them,task:you] You've written for the season's dues, I hear.
[them] Your {OFFICE} has written for the season's dues.
[us] It's the season for it.
[them,vassal:heavy] On top of the harvest cart, it's a lot to find.
[them] The carter will bring what's owed, one way or another.
[them] You're the one who writes for the dues, aren't you?
[us] Someone has to, and the council chose me.
[them] Our head says your letters are polite, at least.
[them,task:you] Our head grumbles every time your letter comes, then calls for the carter.
[them] Our head grumbles every time your {OFFICE}'s letter comes, then calls for the carter.
[us] Grumbling's allowed.
[them] Good, because there's plenty of it.
[us] Our elders gave {OFFICER} this errand, and {OFFICER} doesn't drop an errand.
[them,their:tribal] Our elders do the same, and the young ones run until their feet bleed.
[them] Errands between our peoples are a good thing.
[us] {OFFICER} holds the {OFFICE}'s seat on our council, and takes it seriously.
[them] Good, a seat taken lightly is worse than an empty one.
[us] On our committee, your people are {OFFICER}'s portfolio.
[them,their:industrial] Then {OFFICER} has a thick file, I'm afraid.
[them] I didn't know we were anyone's portfolio.
[us] Your people fall within {OFFICER}'s remit on our board.
[them,their:spacer] Then we'll route everything through {OFFICER}.
[them] Whatever that means, I hope it's good for us.
[them] Your {OFFICE}'s letters are received in our hall as an envoy would be.
[us] {OFFICER} will be glad to hear it.
[them] They're read standing, which is more than most get.
[them] Our committee has your {OFFICE}'s business on the agenda at every meeting now.
[us] Is that good?
[them] It means somebody reads what {OFFICER} sends.
[them] Your colony writes to us a great deal.
[us] We'd rather write than not.
[them] Some of us would rather you didn't.
[them,task:you] People at home still talk about your visit.
[them] People at home still talk about your {OFFICE}'s visit.
[us,task:you] Good things, I hope, I tried to mind my manners.
[us] Good things, I hope.
[them] Mostly good, and the rest was funny.
[them,task:you] You came all the way to us, and it's no short road.
[them] Your {OFFICE} came all the way to us, and it's no short road.
[us,task:you] I felt every hill of it, coming home.
[us] {OFFICER} told us about every hill of it.
[them] Our people noticed the effort.
[them] You're the {OFFICE}, so take this home with you: we don't care for your letters.
[us] I'll take it home.
[them,task:you] We talked about faith last time, and now you write to our head about it.
[them] We talked about faith last time, and now your {OFFICE} writes to our head about it.
[us] We took that talk seriously.
[them] So did our head, though not the way you'd like.
[them,task:you] The fighting with {THEN} goes on, so your drill comes at a good time.
[them] The fighting with {THEN} goes on, so your {OFFICE}'s drill comes at a good time.
[us,task:you] Then I'll make the day count.
[us] Then {OFFICER} will make the day count.
[them] Our fighters are counting on it.
[them,task:you] {THEN} is still with us, so whatever you can sell us, we need.
[them] {THEN} is still with us, so whatever your {OFFICE} can sell us, we need.
[us] Food first, then.
[them] Food first, and at a price we can pay.
[us,task:you] I mean to bring your people medicine, is {THEN} still unwell?
[us] Our {OFFICE} means to bring your people medicine, is {THEN} still unwell?
[them] Still unwell, and glad to hear it.
[us,task:you] Then I'll pack extra.
[us] Then I'll tell {OFFICER} to pack extra.
